ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on the Fight against Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Anti-Money Laundering Act, AMLA) of 10 October 1997 (SR 955.0) as amended, Art. 4 (UBO identification); Financial Services Act (FinSA) of 15 June 2018 (SR 950.1) Art. 52 and 53; Financial Services Ordinance (FinSO) of 6 November 2019 (SR 950.11) Art. 51; Swiss Code of Obligations (CO) of 30 March 1911 (SR 220) Art. 697i (register of beneficial owners of bearer shares); Federal Act on the Enforcement of International Economic Measures (Embargo Act, SR 946.231) and implementing SECO ordinances.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of beneficial owner's valid passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority in the owner's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization at Swiss embassy/consulate (depending on Hague membership of origin state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the owner's jurisdiction of legal residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (if the origin state is not a party to the Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution in the country of origin of the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of bank officer plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if required by the Swiss notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (if any corporate shareholder is involved)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent authority of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under AMLA and FINMA Circular 2016/1 for any politically exposed person (PEP) as defined by FATF. All beneficial owners, directors, and signatories must be screened against the UN sanctions list, EU consolidated list, US OFAC list, and the Swiss SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) sanctions lists and domestic counter-terrorism designations. Screening must be documented and retained for at least ten years; any positive hit requires suspension and a report to the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch) and the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must comply with Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 950 and Art. 951. The name must be in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian) or Romansh, and may include a secondary descriptive element in another language. Non-Latin script names are not admitted; foreign words must be transliterated into Latin script. The name must include the legal form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' (or 'AG' in German, 'SA' in French/Italian) and must not be misleading, contrary to public policy, or infringe third-party rights.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss (requires federal authorization to indicate Swiss character)
Canton (likely to imply official cantonal authority)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Commercial Register Office rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection within 20 days to the cantonal supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde für Handelsregister), citing the statutory non-infringement and clarity grounds and attaching the rejection notice. If the supervisory authority upholds the rejection, an appeal may be lodged with the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days. Alternatively, the applicant may promptly submit a revised name to the registry, which is the fastest commercially prudent remedy; further legal appeal runs parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered address for a manufacturing AG. The company must maintain a physical registered office in a Swiss canton with an actual desk, postal address, and access to corporate records. For the dental ceramic block manufacturing activity, the registered office must reflect a genuine operational facility or, at a minimum, a substantive administrative office located separately from the production site. Virtual office services may be accepted only as additional administrative auxiliary addresses, not as an alternative to demonstrable substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% probability per year of an unannounced on-site inspection by Swiss tax authorities, social insurance authorities, or customs for a standard-risk dental consumables manufacturer. Unannounced commercial register inspections are not established practice; however, a targeted substance audit may occur if the company is flagged as a shell risk or if AML red flags are raised.

Notarial authentic deed of incorporation including certified articles of association (Statuten)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notary tariff (approximately CHF 1,300, varies by canton)

Official publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
Apostille of consular legalization for foreign identity and corporate documents (per bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent cantonal authority for apostille or Swiss consulate / foreign consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per document (USD 100–180 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation into the official language (German, French, or Italian) of foreign company documents and powers of attorney
UBO/PEP/OFAC/UN and SECO sanctions screening and AML dossier compilation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a low-risk manufacturer (USD 600–800 flat fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate (hourly or fixed fee; estimated CHF 2,500)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR; SR 220), Fifth Part, Articles 620–763, in particular Article 626 (minimum nominal capital of CHF 100,000), Article 627 (mandatory content of the Articles of Association), Article 632 (minimum paid-up cash capital and blocking requirement), Article 634 (in-kind contribution report), Article 640 (commercial register filings) and Article 698 (general meeting); supplemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV; SR 221.411) and, for the regulated product scope, the Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO; SR 812.213).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) at the registered seat of the company, under the functional supervision of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Amt für das Handelsregister, EHR) of the Federal Office of Justice; electronic filing via the eGRIS platform and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister — Application for Entry in the Commercial Register, filed together with the notarized deed of incorporation and the Articles of Association (Statuten).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Aktiengesellschaft requires a minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 (approx. USD 112,000). At least CHF 20,000 (20% of the nominal capital) must be paid up in cash on a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) opened in the company's name at a licensed Swiss bank or financial intermediary before registration; the bank's confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung) that the funds are at the company's free disposal must accompany the application, and the funds are released to the Board only after the constitutive Commercial Register entry. In-kind contributions require a special audit report under Article 634 OR.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the founders' subscription to the entire nominal share capital of CHF 100,000, fully paid in cash pursuant to Art. 632 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, is approved, ratified, and allotted to the subscribers named in the deed. 2. That the Company's registered office is hereby adopted at the domicile specified in the Articles of Association, Canton of Zurich, Switzerland. 3. That the following persons shall be and are hereby appointed as Board members and signatory officers: [Name], Chairman, with individual signatory authority (Einzelunterschrift); [Name], Secretary. 4. That the Board of Directors is irrevocably authorized to lodge the Commercial Register application, open company bank accounts, and take all necessary steps to obtain the Company's statutory industrial licenses.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC) for federal taxes and VAT; cantonal tax authorities for cantonal/communal corporate taxes. Portal: www.estv.admin.ch and SwissTax Online e-services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) in the Swiss Commercial Register; the Federal Statistical Office automatically issues the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx). 2. Apply for VAT registration with the ESTV via the official VAT registration form or SwissTax e-portal, specifying the dental ceramic block manufacturing activity (ISIC 3250) and the expected Swiss taxable turnover. 3. ESTV validates the application and issues the MWST/TVA/IVA VAT number linked to the UID. 4. Foreign-incorporated entities supplying taxable goods or services in Switzerland must register for Swiss VAT in their own name, appoint a Swiss tax representative/fiscal domiciliary if no Swiss establishment exists, and obtain a Swiss VAT identification number. 5. In parallel, register with the cantonal compensation office for old-age/social insurance employer obligations and obtain an employer number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or pass-through election exists. An AG is automatically an independent taxable person subject to Swiss federal, cantonal and communal corporate income tax. Statutory election mechanisms available include the Qualified Participation Deduction for dividends and capital gains on qualifying qualifying participations, the election for Swiss VAT group registration under Art. 21 VAT Act, partial VAT deduction election for real estate, and the deemed liquidation election on relocation/emigration under Swiss international taxation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / MWST / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies for Swiss-resident businesses (Art. 10 VAT Act); non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Switzerland are subject to VAT regardless of any threshold and must register or appoint a fiscal representative unless an exemption applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government clearance API, or mandatory digital stamping is currently required for Swiss VAT e-invoicing. Electronic invoices are permissible if authenticity, integrity and readability are guaranteed for the 10-year retention period. Domestic payment and e-billing may use the Swiss QR-bill standard, but the ESTV does not require pre-approval of invoices through a national clearance portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0% VAT) applies to the physical export of dental CAD/CAM zirconia blocks sold by a Swiss taxable person to a foreign buyer, provided the goods are transported directly from Switzerland to a foreign destination, the exporter retains a valid customs export declaration, the goods leave Switzerland unconditionally and definitively, and the export transaction is recorded in the seller's business records. The export must be supported within the statutory deadline by customs and transport evidence; the recipient must not be domiciled in Switzerland and the commercial terms must place transfer of ownership abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Ausfuhrdeklaration validated by the Swiss Federal Customs Administration (BAZG / EZV), including the export transaction number (NCTS/export accompanying document)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill or CMR road consignment note showing physical dispatch from Switzerland to a foreign destination
Commercial invoice for the dental zirconia blocks (ISIC 3250) indicating 0% VAT and the exporter's Swiss VAT ID
Packing list, purchase order, and export sales contract evidencing the foreign buyer and delivery terms
Bank SWIFT wire or TT payment credit advice, or an Inward Remittance Certificate from the Swiss bank, proving actual receipt of the foreign currency proceeds from the non-resident buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export zero-rating cannot be substantiated with valid customs and logistics documents, the VAT has to be retrospectively assessed at 8.1% plus statutory default interest from the date of supply. Knowingly false export declarations or fictitious documents trigger criminal proceedings under Art. 82-85 of the Swiss VAT Act and the Federal Customs Act, with fines up to CHF 30,000 or imprisonment for aggravated tax fraud, forfeiture of the tax advantage, denial/recovery of input VAT deductions, and, in serious cases, an administrative penalty not exceeding three times the evaded VAT. In addition, legal and beneficial ownership of the goods and SWIFT/TT payment provenance are scrutinized to counter sham exports and circular cash flows.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), Schweizerische Nationalbank, with banking supervision under the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. Switzerland maintains no exchange controls, no prior-approval requirements for profit repatriation, and no restrictions on dividend or capital transfers. Cross-border payments in CHF, EUR, and USD are free-flowing; the only friction is the 35% Swiss anticipatory withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends, which is fully or partially reclaimable under applicable double taxation treaties. No convertibility hurdles, no negative interest regime at present.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory timeline for the surrender of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio into CHF. Exporters may freely retain, credit, or convert foreign currency receipts. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations to the SNB apply for quarterly transactions above CHF 10 million or annual turnover thresholds; no treasury restriction is triggered.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility for Swiss FINMA-licensed fintech institutions operating under Art. 1b Banking Act (Fintech/Sandbox license), which may hold public deposits up to CHF 100 million without full banking license. Offshore foreign EMIs without Swiss FINMA supervision are practically non-viable: Swiss banks routinely decline to serve as correspondent for unsupervised EMIs, and mandated Anti-Money Laundering representatives are unwilling to accept liability for non-supervised beneficiaries.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under FINMA Circular 2016/07 via recorded video identification for pure Swiss and certain EU/UK residents, but for a non-resident-owned AG, banks normally require at least one physical interview of the ultimate beneficial owner and the mandated signatory—either at the bank's premises, a Swiss notary, or a Swiss embassy/consulate. Full remote opening is available only when all directors are Swiss residents with SwissID or when the bank approves a trusted-qualified electronic signature; practical recommendation: one face-to-face closing meeting in Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership with opaque chain through an offshore vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational chart of the full ownership chain; commercial registry extract (Handelsregisterauszug) not older than 3 months; audited financial statements of the parent company; passports and proof of residential address of all shareholders above 25%; professional references from a regulated foreign bank; negative media and sanctions screening report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance in Switzerland for the manufacturing AG
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Swiss lease agreement for registered office; sworn declaration of the registered office (Sitzbestätigung); payroll records and social insurance confirmations of Swiss personnel; board meeting minutes held in Switzerland; Swiss VAT registration certificate; detailed business plan evidencing warehousing, distribution, and invoicing from Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of initial share capital or escrowed capital contribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the contributing entity; source bank account statements covering the previous 12 months; signed capital payment instruction and notarised deed of incorporation; proof of earnings (tax returns, sales contracts, dividend resolutions); declaration of source of wealth with documentary evidence of accumulated funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed as statutory paid-in capital: funds wired via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'GDSK' or 'INVC' into a designated capital escrow account (Sperrkonto) prescribed by the Swiss notary; the bank verifies the share subscription agreement, notarised deed, and board capital payment resolution against the wire before releasing credit to the operating account. No SNB approval required; any currency is accepted, with conversion at prevailing market rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails are SWIFT MT103/MT202 for direct telegraphic transfers; high-value auto-clearing through Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) for CHF; SEPA CT for EUR pool disbursements; documentary collections (CAD) and irrevocable confirmed letters of credit (MT700/MT710) are standard for export of dental ceramic blocks where payment risk mitigation is required. Trade-finance disbursements require invoice, packing list, bill of lading/AWB, and certificate of origin for compliance review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX outright forwards (maturity up to 12 months standard; documentation under ISDA 2002 or Swiss Master Agreement for OTC Derivatives)
FX swaps (swap-effective netting under banks' ISDA/CSA framework)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term CHF-denominated intercompany financing
Vanilla FX options (epsilon-based or European-style, cash-settled)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on convertible currencies (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF) available from major counterparties, though low market depth as CHF is fully deliverable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory auditor's report (if compulsory) — Jahresrechnung
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) — required only when the company is subject to an ordinary audit; otherwise retained at the registered office and not publicly filed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The shareholders' meeting must approve the financial statements within 6 months after the financial year-end; if publication is mandatory, the Commercial Register must receive the statements within 12 months after that year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Switzerland has no administrative strike-off mechanism. A shareholder, creditor or the Commercial Register may petition the court for an order to remedy; continued non-compliance can result in judicial dissolution under Article 731b of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions_timeline: Court proceedings typically commence 30 days after a formal default notice; no automatic administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and capital tax return (federal, cantonal and municipal direct taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and the Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV) as supervisory authority; the return is filed with the cantonal tax authorities for federal, cantonal and municipal purposes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The tax return is due within 6 months after the end of the business year, or the period stated in the cantonal filing notice — commonly 30 June for calendar-year taxpayers; administrative extensions are available on request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a fine of up to 30% of the assessed tax and late interest at 5% per annum; persistent default after formal reminders leads to an estimated assessment and, in cases of wilful evasion, criminal tax prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The filing interval is set by ESTV, generally quarterly or six-monthly, with returns due within 60 days after the expiry of the VAT period; an annual VAT return is admissible only if expressly approved by ESTV, in which case the deadline remains 60 days after the calendar year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late returns may incur a default surcharge of up to 5% of the tax due plus arrears interest at 5% per annum; deliberate VAT evasion is subject to a fine of up to three times the tax evaded and criminal proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft must appoint a statutory auditor and provide an ordinary audit (ordentliche Prüfung) if it exceeds two of the following thresholds in two consecutive business years: total assets above CHF 20 million; net annual turnover above CHF 40 million; annual average of 250 full-time employees. Where these thresholds are not met, a limited audit (eingeschränkte Prüfung) is mandatory unless the company and its group employ fewer than 10 full-time employees on average per year and all shareholders agree in writing to waive the audit for each financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The annual accounts must comply with the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR); accounting principles may be presented under Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS. IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements or as a voluntary supplementary presentation, but the statutory annual financial statements of a non-listed AG remain governed by OR / Swiss GAAP FER.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not require an annual declaration of beneficial owners to a central authority. Under Article 697j of the Swiss Code of Obligations, the company must continuously maintain an internal register of beneficial owners (UBO-Register) and update it within 14 days after any change in qualified shareholding or transfer of registered shares. At each annual shareholders' meeting, the board of directors confirms in the minutes that the share register (Aktienbuch) and the UBO register are accurate and complete; this confirmation is not filed with the Commercial Register. Transfers of registered shares are recorded in the share register only after the board approves the corresponding entry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 1,800 per year for a registered office and corporate agent service at a commercial address in Switzerland, excluding cantonal register fees and courier costs.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 7,500 per year for a limited audit (vereinfachte Prüfung); USD 12,000 – USD 35,000 per year for an ordinary audit (ordentliche Prüfung) of a mid-sized non-listed Aktiengesellschaft.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal direct corporate income tax assessed on post-tax net profit (equivalent to 7.83% of pre-tax profit); combined with cantonal and communal profit taxes in the Canton of Zug, total effective burden approx. 14.6% of pre-tax profit (2024-2025 published rate for the municipality of Zug, including federal direct tax, after capital tax offset).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; preferential deductions under the Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF), effective since 1 January 2020: (i) Patent Box: up to 90% reduction of qualifying income from patents and equivalent protected rights, applicable at cantonal level (not for federal direct tax); (ii) R&D super deduction: additional 50% deduction for Swiss R&D personnel and contracted R&D; (iii) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on excess equity where introduced by the canton; (iv) participation exemption for dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings of at least 10%; (v) old cantonal status regimes abolished, with transition periods ended.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Federal and Cantonal Corporate Income Tax Return for Legal Entities (Formular B in the Canton of Zug); e-filed via the DIAMANT electronic declaration portal of the Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug, which simultaneously assesses federal direct tax and cantonal/communal profit tax; the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) receives data by exchange of information.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within six months after the close of the statutory business year (Art. 125-126 Federal Act on Direct Taxes, DBG); for a company with a 31 December year-end, the ordinary deadline is 30 June of the following year, with individual extensions routinely granted upon non-taxable request until 31 October; further extension only upon written motion showing grounds. Tax is assessed by notice of assessment and is not self-assessed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, commercial register number, UID/MWST number, registered seat, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft), share capital, purpose, balance-sheet date, board members, authorised signatories and full list of shareholders with nationality and residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and foreign directors must be identified with their foreign tax registration numbers and country of residence. A domestic service-of-process address and an authorised Swiss representative must be entered. The foreign parent must be disclosed even where no direct Swiss holding is registered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss as stated in the Swiss statutory annual financial statements and approved by the shareholders' meeting; for the dental CAD/CAM business this is revenue from zirconia block and milling disc sales less raw material, production, R&D, distribution and administrative costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases of zirconia powder or prefabricated blanks from a foreign affiliate must be supported by written agreements and priced at arm's length; patents or trademark licences paid to a foreign parent must be justified and disclosed in the annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses under Art. 59-62 DBG: proportional portion of Swiss 35% anticipatory tax on financial income, non-business-related donations exceeding the statutory cap, tax portions, asset-step-up depreciation and half of bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No direct foreign-shareholder entry; the AG must add back foreign withholding tax on dividends received from its own foreign subsidiaries unless covered by the participation exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from shareholdings of at least 10% of nominal or share capital held for at least one year; effective exemption rate of at least 92.15% (federal) and 100% (most cantons, incl. Zug) after cost add-back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The participation exemption is assessed at the level of the filing AG only; a foreign parent may not offset any Swiss participation income within the AG return. A foreign parent holding at least 10% of the AG must nonetheless be reported in the annexes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal deduction of up to 90% of net qualifying income from Swiss or foreign patents and equivalent rights, including patented zirconia material compositions and CAD/CAM software method patents, applying the nexus-access factor based on R&D expenditure ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If qualifying IP was acquired from or developed jointly with a foreign parent, a full transfer pricing study, patent registration extracts and R&D expense allocation per nexus rules must be attached; failure to do so triggers reclassification and reassessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional deduction of 50% of qualifying Swiss R&D personnel costs and up to 80% of mandated third-party R&D expenditures, capped at 80% of total deductible R&D base; also granted at federal level subject to the same conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D invoices from the foreign parent are eligible only where the Swiss AG exercises substantive technical supervision; supporting time studies, project protocols and employment contracts of Swiss R&D staff must be retained for field audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit plus additions minus deductions, constituting the taxable basis for federal direct tax at 8.5% and for Zug cantonal/communal profit tax at the combined statutory rate; taxable profit is declared gross before tax deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable profit belongs solely to the Swiss AG; no part may be attributed directly to foreign shareholders. Foreign directors must ensure the profit is justified by locally performed functions, assets and risks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Taxable Equity and Loss Utilisation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal capital tax base (taxable equity, reduced by participations and qualifying intangibles) and the deduction of prior-year tax losses; losses may be carried forward for a maximum of 7 years per Art. 211 DBG and art. 27 of the Zug Tax Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss utilisation survives a change of foreign ownership unless the acquisition was structured to obtain a tax advantage with no business purpose; the Zug tax authority may deny loss carryforward where a loss-making shell was acquired from non-residents without operational continuity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174 DBG; for negligent understatement, penalty up to 30% of the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG); intentional concealment: fine of 1-3 times the evaded amount; default assessment by the Zug tax authority adds a 10% surcharge and procedural costs up to CHF 2,000; arrears interest on unpaid tax accrues at approx. 4.0-4.5% per annum until payment. There is no statutory daily surcharge, but monthly compounding of arrears interest applies.
